passage: The Abara group investigated turnover of p53, a regulatory protein that is rapidly degraded in proliferating cells. To measure stability without confounding new synthesis, cells were treated with cycloheximide, an inhibitor of translation elongation, and harvested at the times shown. Lysates were resolved by SDS-PAGE, transferred to a membrane, and probed with an antibody against p53; band intensities were quantified and normalized to a loading control. Degradation of p53 was assumed to follow first-order kinetics. The researchers hoped to compare half-lives under normal and stressed conditions and to learn whether proteasome inhibition would stabilize the protein. Results from unstressed cells are shown; each value is the mean of three biological replicates, with errors below 5% of the mean. Equal total protein was loaded in every lane, as confirmed by the loading control. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What fraction of p53 remains 40 minutes after cycloheximide treatment?
questions.explanation: At 40 min, two half-lives have elapsed (100 → 50 → 25%).
questions.trap: Treating decay as linear and choosing 75%; two half-lives of 20 min leave 25%, not 75%.

questions.stem: Why is cycloheximide used in this experiment?

options.A: It blocks new synthesis so that the loss of existing protein can be followed
options.B: It increases transcription of the gene
options.C: It labels the protein for detection by antibody
options.D: It accelerates proteasomal degradation of all proteins

questions.explanation: Without blocking translation, newly synthesized protein would obscure the decay of the pre-existing pool.
questions.trap: Thinking cycloheximide raises transcription, labels the protein or speeds degradation; it only blocks translation so decay of the existing pool can be followed.

questions.stem: If the decay continues to be first-order, what percentage of p53 remains after 80 minutes?
questions.trap: Reporting the fraction lost (93.75%) or miscounting half-lives (12.5% is 3 half-lives, 3.125% is 5) instead of 4 half-lives, 6.25%.

questions.stem: Which statement about first-order decay is INCORRECT?

options.A: The rate of decay is proportional to the amount remaining
options.B: The half-life equals ln 2 divided by the rate constant
options.C: The half-life increases as the starting amount of protein increases
options.D: The half-life is independent of starting concentration

questions.explanation: In first-order kinetics, t½ = ln 2/k and does not depend on starting concentration.
questions.trap: Believing first-order half-life depends on the starting amount; it is constant and equals ln 2 divided by k.

questions.stem: p53 turnover is typically controlled by which system?

options.A: Glycosylation in the Golgi apparatus that prevents degradation
options.C: Phosphorylation by glycolytic kinases that leads to secretion
options.D: Ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome

questions.explanation: Polyubiquitin chains (K48-linked) mark proteins for proteasomal degradation; proteasome inhibitors such as MG132 stabilize short-lived regulatory proteins.
questions.trap: Choosing Golgi glycosylation, lysosomal ribosome degradation or kinase-driven secretion; p53 stability is controlled by ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.
